correctness.rationale: The first-flip event of a lone opinion-1 hub can be killed while replacing the hub with an opinion-1 frozen source. Private clique blades are then independent and hub copying from zero neighbors is a Poisson thinning of total rate ∑Z_i(t)/L. Thus no flip to all-1 absorption equals product of blade integrated-exposure Laplace transforms f_{r_i}(1/L). For a size-r blade the zero count jumps down at z(r-z+1)/r and up at z(r-z)/r; finite-state Feynman–Kac gives tridiagonal B_r(t), f_r(t)=(r!)²/(r^r det B_r(t)). Generator applied to z is -z/r, whence E∫Zdt=r², and uniform finite-state second moments for r≤R yield log p=-∑r_i²/L+O_R(1/L). Independently reconstructed full labelled voter generators and exact rational inversions for blades (1),(2),(1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(1,1,2) yield respectively 1/2,2/7,4/9,27/92,64/289,128/425, matching determinants. The bounded-r asymptotic requires bounded blade sizes; finite cases are corroborative, not a proof.

value.rationale: The finite product determines an important pathwise persistence statistic (no reversal) on a natural one-hub family, not merely average final consensus. The size-biased mean ∑r_i²/L explains the sharp e^-r hierarchy under fixed hub degree, revealing that adding only peripheral edges changes the no-flip limit; this is a motivated exact structural and scaling law beyond a textbook fixation result.

limitations: Only one initially dissenting hub, ordinary binary voter dynamics; bounded blade-size asymptotic cannot be extended to growing sizes without new analysis.
Historical priority limited by potentially unexamined graph-persistence formulas.
